g.text: In recent years, deep neural networks have achieved remarkable success
across a wide range of applications.
g.title: N1 [Context] (cites=0) In recent years, deep neural networks have achieved remarkable success across a wide range of applications.

g.text: Among these advancements, Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs)
(Chen et al., 2018b) stand out due to their continuous nature and parameter
g.title: N2 [Context] (cites=1) Among these advancements, Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) (Chen et al., 2018b) stand out due to their continuous nature and parameter efficiency through shared parameters.

g.text: Unlike conventional neural networks with discrete layers, Neural ODEs model
the evolution of hidden states as a continuous-time differential equation,
allowing them to better capture dynamic systems.
g.title: N3 [Context] (cites=0) Unlike conventional neural networks with discrete layers, Neural ODEs model the evolution of hidden states as a continuous-time differential equation, allowing them to better capture dynamic systems.

g.text: shared params: consistent dynamics, less memory
This parameter-sharing mechanism ensures consistent dynamics throughout the
continuous transformation and reduces the number of parameters, improving
both memory efficiency and computational complexity.
g.title: N4 [Context] (cites=0) This parameter-sharing mechanism ensures consistent dynamics throughout the continuous transformation and reduces the number of parameters, improving both memory efficiency and computational complexity.

g.text: These unique properties make Neural ODEs particularly effective not only for
traditional machine learning tasks like image classification (Chen et al.,
2018b) and natural language processing (Rubanova et al., 2019), but also for
g.title: N5 [Context] (cites=5) These unique properties make Neural ODEs particularly effective not only for traditional machine learning tasks like image classification (Chen et al., 2018b) and natural language processing (Rubanova et al., 2019), but also for more complex tasks involving continuous processes, such as time series analysis (Kidger et al., 2020), reinforcement learning (Du et al., 2020), and diffusion models (Song et al., 2020).

g.text: However, while these features offer flexibility and efficiency,
they also introduce significant challenges during training,
particularly in gradient computation and convergence analysis.
g.title: N6 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, while these features offer flexibility and efficiency, they also introduce significant challenges during training, particularly in gradient computation and convergence analysis.

g.text: One of the key challenges in training Neural ODEs is accurately
g.title: N7 [Limitation: challenge-1] (cites=0) One of the key challenges in training Neural ODEs is accurately computing gradients.

g.text: Unlike traditional networks, where backpropagation can be computed
through a discrete chain of layers, Neural ODEs require solving
forward and backward ODEs using numerical solvers.
g.title: N8 [Limitation] (cites=0) Unlike traditional networks, where backpropagation can be computed through a discrete chain of layers, Neural ODEs require solving forward and backward ODEs using numerical solvers.

g.text: These solvers introduce numerical errors, which can lead to inaccurate
gradients and slow convergence or even suboptimal model performance
g.title: N9 [Limitation] (cites=1) These solvers introduce numerical errors, which can lead to inaccurate gradients and slow convergence or even suboptimal model performance (Rodriguez et al., 2022).

g.text: Moreover, ensuring the well-posedness of ODE solutions during training is
g.title: N10 [Limitation] (cites=0) Moreover, ensuring the well-posedness of ODE solutions during training is nontrivial.

g.text: Picard-Lindelof: solutions may be local only
According to the Picard–Lindelöf Theorem, solutions may not always
exist or may only exist locally, which can cause training
divergence or significant numerical errors (Gholami et al., 2019;
Ott et al., 2020; Sander et al., 2022).
g.title: N11 [Prior_Work] (cites=3) According to the Picard–Lindelöf Theorem, solutions may not always exist or may only exist locally, which can cause training divergence or significant numerical errors (Gholami et al., 2019; Ott et al., 2020; Sander et al., 2022).

g.text: open: can SGD train Neural ODEs reliably?
Even with advanced solvers (Zhuang et al., 2020a;b; Matsubara et
al., 2021; Ko et al., 2023), it remains an open problem whether
simple first-order methods, such as stochastic gradient descent
(SGD), can reliably train Neural ODEs to…
g.title: N12 [Limitation] (cites=4) Even with advanced solvers (Zhuang et al., 2020a;b; Matsubara et al., 2021; Ko et al., 2023), it remains an open problem whether simple first-order methods, such as stochastic gradient descent (SGD), can reliably train Neural ODEs to convergence.

g.text: discretization gradients may not match continuous
While discretizing Neural ODEs as finite-depth networks offers a
potential solution, it results in a deeper computation graph
(Zhuang et al., 2020a;b), raising questions about whether the
gradients computed in this manner truly match those…
g.title: N13 [Limitation] (cites=2) While discretizing Neural ODEs as finite-depth networks offers a potential solution, it results in a deeper computation graph (Zhuang et al., 2020a;b), raising questions about whether the gradients computed in this manner truly match those of the continuous model.

g.text: Another essential challenge lies in analyzing the training
g.title: N14 [Limitation: challenge-2] (cites=0) Another essential challenge lies in analyzing the training dynamics of Neural ODEs.

g.text: nonconvex optimization is hard to analyze
The optimization problem in training neural networks is inherently
g.title: N15 [Limitation] (cites=0) The optimization problem in training neural networks is inherently nonconvex, making theoretical analysis difficult.

g.text: Jacot et al.: NTK converges as width grows
Recent work by Jacot et al. (2018) has shown that the training
dynamics of overparameterized networks can be understood through
the lens of the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK), which converges to a
g.title: N16 [Prior_Work] (cites=1) Recent work by Jacot et al. (2018) has shown that the training dynamics of overparameterized networks can be understood through the lens of the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK), which converges to a deterministic limit as network width increases.

g.text: This convergence has enabled researchers to establish global convergence
guarantees for gradient-based methods in overparameterized regimes, provided
the NTK remains strictly positive definite (SPD) (Du et al., 2019a;
g.title: N17 [Prior_Work] (cites=4) This convergence has enabled researchers to establish global convergence guarantees for gradient-based methods in overparameterized regimes, provided the NTK remains strictly positive definite (SPD) (Du et al., 2019a; Allen-Zhu et al., 2019; Nguyen, 2021; Gao et al., 2021).

g.text: dual activation extended to deep finite nets
The analysis of the NTK's strict positive definiteness began with Daniely et
al. (2016), who introduced the concept of dual activation for two-layer
networks, later extended to deeper, finite networks (Jacot et al., 2018; Du
g.title: N18 [Prior_Work] (cites=3) The analysis of the NTK's strict positive definiteness began with Daniely et al. (2016), who introduced the concept of dual activation for two-layer networks, later extended to deeper, finite networks (Jacot et al., 2018; Du et al., 2019a).

g.text: However, these results are limited to networks with discrete
layers, raising the question of whether the same properties hold
for continuous models like Neural ODEs.
g.title: N19 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, these results are limited to networks with discrete layers, raising the question of whether the same properties hold for continuous models like Neural ODEs.

g.text: In this paper, we address these challenges by exploring the impact of
activation functions on training Neural ODEs.
g.title: N20 [Method] (cites=0) In this paper, we address these challenges by exploring the impact of activation functions on training Neural ODEs.

g.text: We show that activation function properties—specifically, smoothness and
nonlinearity—play critical roles in determining the well-posedness of ODE
solutions and the spectral properties of the NTK.
g.title: N21 [Method] (cites=0) We show that activation function properties—specifically, smoothness and nonlinearity—play critical roles in determining the well-posedness of ODE solutions and the spectral properties of the NTK.

g.text: smoothness gives globally unique ODE solutions
Through our analysis, we demonstrate that smooth activation
functions lead to globally unique solutions for both forward and
backward ODEs, ensuring the stability of the training process.
g.title: N22 [Result] (cites=0) Through our analysis, we demonstrate that smooth activation functions lead to globally unique solutions for both forward and backward ODEs, ensuring the stability of the training process.

g.text: extend NTK results to continuous models
Additionally, we extend existing results on the NTK from
discrete-layered neural networks to continuous models,
demonstrating that the NTK for Neural ODEs is well-defined.
g.title: N23 [Result] (cites=0) Additionally, we extend existing results on the NTK from discrete-layered neural networks to continuous models, demonstrating that the NTK for Neural ODEs is well-defined.

g.text: more nonlinearity preserves SPD NTK + speeds convergence
Importantly, we find that a higher degree of nonlinearity in the
activation function not only helps maintain the SPD property of
the limiting NTK, but also practically speeds up Neural ODE
g.title: N24 [Result] (cites=0) Importantly, we find that a higher degree of nonlinearity in the activation function not only helps maintain the SPD property of the limiting NTK, but also practically speeds up Neural ODE convergence.

g.text: We investigate the significance of the smoothness of
activation functions for the well-posedness of forward
and backward ODEs in Neural ODEs.
g.title: N25 [Contribution] (cites=0) We investigate the significance of the smoothness of activation functions for the well-posedness of forward and backward ODEs in Neural ODEs.
N26 [Contribution] (cites=0) Using random matrix theory, we demonstrate the existence of globally unique solutions.
N27 [Contribution] (cites=0) Additionally, we show that no additional regularity is needed if forward and backward ODEs are combined in a weakly coupled ODE system.

g.text: We propose a new mathematical framework for studying
continuous models from the approximation theory
g.title: N28 [Contribution] (cites=0) We propose a new mathematical framework for studying continuous models from the approximation theory perspective.

N29 [Contribution] (cites=0) By using a sequence of finite-depth neural networks to approximate Neural ODEs, we show that key properties like activation and gradient propagation are preserved as depth approaches infinity.
N30 [Contribution] (cites=0) This allows us to apply the Moore-Osgood theorem from functional analysis to prove that the NTK of Neural ODEs is well-defined.

g.text: Contribution 3: SPD may fail at infinite depth
Unfortunately, the SPD property of the NTK may not hold
at infinite depth, even we can show every finite-depth
g.title: N31 [Contribution] (cites=0) Unfortunately, the SPD property of the NTK may not hold at infinite depth, even we can show every finite-depth approximation satisfies it.
N32 [Contribution] (cites=0) To address this, we conduct a fine-grained analysis and derive an integral form for the limiting NTK of Neural ODEs.
N33 [Contribution] (cites=0) This form reveals that the NTK remains SPD if the activation function is non-polynomial.
N34 [Contribution] (cites=0) Leveraging this integral representation provides valuable insights into continuous models and may inspire further research.

g.text: We conduct a series of numerical experiments to support
g.title: N35 [Contribution] (cites=0) We conduct a series of numerical experiments to support our theoretical findings.
N36 [Contribution] (cites=0) Beyond validating our analysis, these experiments also provide practical guidelines for training Neural ODEs.
N37 [Contribution] (cites=0) We show that activation function smoothness and nonlinearity accelerate convergence and improve performance (see Figure 7-8).

N38 [Contribution] (cites=0) Conversely, improper ODE scaling leads to damping from accumulated numerical errors (see Figure3), while adaptive solvers struggle with efficiency in large-scale Neural ODEs (see Figure 14), causing instability and high computational overhead.
